scenario.description: Three internal systems (Student Affairs, Finance, Facilities) and three outside APIs (Open-Meteo, Nager.Date, Frankfurter) must work together to plan one event request.

scale: 1 = poor, 5 = very good. For cost, 5 = cheap and quick to build, 1 = expensive and slow.

cost.why: a small student team with one semester

options.name: Point-to-point
options.idea: Each system calls each other system directly.

why.performance: one direct call, no extra hop
why.maintainability: 6 systems need up to 15 links, and each one is code to maintain
why.interoperability: every link may use its own format
why.cost: cheap while there are few links

options.name: Hub-and-spoke (API gateway)
options.idea: Every call goes through one gateway that knows all the systems.

why.security: one place for validation and logging
why.reliability: timeouts and retries are written once
why.availability: the hub is a single point of failure

options.name: Enterprise service bus (ESB)
options.idea: A central bus routes, transforms and orchestrates messages between many systems.

why.capacity: built for many systems and heavy traffic
why.cost: a product to buy or learn, and a lot of configuration
why.performance: every message passes the bus and its transformations

options.name: Batch file transfer (ETL)
options.idea: Files are extracted, transformed and loaded on a schedule, for example every night.

why.performance: an answer arrives with the next run, not within 3 seconds
why.usability: the organizer waits for the next run
why.capacity: large volumes in one run are what batch does well

options.name: Event-driven (message queue)
options.idea: Systems publish events to a queue; others consume them when they are ready.

why.availability: a consumer that is down just reads later
why.reliability: messages wait in the queue and are retried
why.usability: the organizer gets no direct answer, only a later message

options.name: Gateway + queue for notifications
options.idea: A gateway answers the organizer at once; the notice about the decision goes through a message queue.

why.availability: the answer does not wait for the mail system; the queue holds the notice
why.reliability: failed notices are retried from the queue
why.maintainability: two parts to maintain instead of one
why.cost: a gateway plus a small in-memory queue
